title: A telescope helps us look far away

body.heading: Super eyes for the sky
paragraphs: A telescope makes far away things look bigger. Point it at the Moon and you can see bumps and shadows that your eyes alone cannot see.
Long ago, a man named Galileo looked through a telescope and saw that the Moon is not smooth like a ball. It has mountains, just like Earth!

body.heading: Looking together
paragraphs: Telescopes work best on a clear, dark night. Take turns to look, and tell each other what you see. The Moon is a good first thing to find, because it is big and bright.
Never point a telescope at the Sun. The Sun is far too bright and can hurt eyes badly. Telescopes are for the night sky only.

takeaway: A telescope makes far things look bigger, so you can see the Moon's mountains — but never look at the Sun through one.
